planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade with shelter from hot afternoon sun; Whitewater is grown primarily for its marbled foliage rather than flowers.

directions: Plant in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun, in moist, well-drained soil; Whitewater is a patented variegated sport of bear's breeches bearing bold, deeply lobed leaves marbled in white and green, grown as an architectural foliage accent rather than for its flower spikes. It makes a striking specimen in a shaded border or large container where the pale variegation shows up well against darker companion plantings. Mulch well and provide winter protection at the colder end of its range, since variegated sports can be slightly less cold-hardy than the plain species.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade; Sparkles needs steady moisture to perform well as a compact woodland-border perennial.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in consistently moist, humus-rich soil; Sparkles is a compact dwarf goat's beard selection bearing creamy, plume-like flower spikes above finely cut, ferny foliage from late spring into summer. Its small scale suits shaded rock gardens and woodland-border edges where the larger species Aruncus dioicus would be out of proportion. Keep soil from drying out through summer, especially in warmer parts of its range, and divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil in partial shade under deciduous tree canopy; masterwort tolerates dappled light well once established.

directions: Plant in partial shade under deciduous canopy in humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil; masterwort carries its small domed flower clusters inside papery, pincushion-like bracts, held on wiry stems above mounded foliage from early to midsummer. Masterpiece is valued for richly colored bracts that hold up well both in the garden and as a cut flower. It self-sows modestly in congenial woodland-edge conditions and benefits from a spring mulch to keep roots cool and moist through summer heat.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil in partial shade; Vanilla Gorilla is a larger-flowered, more vigorous masterwort selection suited to woodland borders with room to spread.

directions: Plant in partial shade in humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil; Vanilla Gorilla is a vigorous, larger-flowered masterwort selection bearing creamy white pincushion blooms over a longer season than many masterwort cultivars, from early summer into fall with deadheading. Its bigger stature and robust habit make it a good anchor plant for a shaded or woodland-edge border where it has some room to fill in. Give it steady moisture through summer and a spring mulch to conserve soil moisture at the root zone.

planting.note: Pot into a warm, humid shaded spot in spring using a light, well-drained mix; Iron Cross Begonia grows best in filtered light with high humidity, like most rhizomatous species begonias.

directions: Grow in shade to filtered light with warm temperatures and high humidity, in a light, well-drained potting mix; Iron Cross Begonia is a species begonia named for the dark cross-shaped marking patterning its leaves, grown chiefly as a foliage specimen for shaded shelves, greenhouses, or terrariums. Keep the soil evenly moist but allow the surface to dry slightly between waterings, and avoid cold drafts, which this tropical species cannot tolerate. It has no outdoor frost hardiness and is grown as a houseplant or warm-greenhouse specimen outside the tropics.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil in shade; Red China is a selection of the hardy Chinese species begonia valued for leaf-color tinting over the straight species.

directions: Plant in shade in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil; Red China is a selection of the hardy, palmately-lobed Chinese woodland species Begonia pedatifida, chosen for leaves that flush with reddish tones beyond the plain green of the straight species. It spreads gradually by rhizome to form an attractive groundcover under shaded woodland plantings in mild-winter climates. Protect it from hard freezes and give it a sheltered, humid site similar to the moist Chinese forest floor it comes from.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; Dumbo's large, rounded, hairy leaves tolerate dry shade once established beneath trees.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in well-drained soil; Dumbo is a large-leaved Bergenia ciliata selection named for its oversized, rounded, softly hairy leaves that give an elephant-ear-like effect in a shaded border. It tolerates dry shade better than most true shade perennials once its root system is established, making it a useful groundcover under established trees. Clusters of small flowers appear in spring above the bold foliage; divide congested clumps every few years to keep the planting vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in evenly moist, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; Winter Glow colors up best with some winter chill to trigger the foliage flush.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in evenly moist, well-drained soil; Winter Glow is a glossy evergreen pigsqueak selection whose rounded, leathery leaves flush with vivid color through cold weather, extending seasonal interest well past its pink spring flower display. It tolerates poor soil and a wide range of shade conditions, making it an easy, low-maintenance groundcover under trees or along a shaded path edge. Division every few years keeps mature clumps looking fresh and encourages the strongest winter color.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in shade to partial shade; top-dress with compost each spring like other members of the Terra Nova Dragonfly bergenia series.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in humus-rich, evenly moist soil; Dragonfly Sakura belongs to Terra Nova Nurseries' Dragonfly series of compact bergenias, carrying pink-flushed spring blooms over leathery evergreen foliage on a smaller-statured plant than species forms. It suits shaded rock gardens and container plantings where its compact size fits better than a full-size pigsqueak. It is deer- and rabbit-resistant and spreads slowly by rhizome; divide congested clumps every four to five years in spring.

common_name: Potsdam Stripe Lily of the Valley

planting.note: Plant pips or divisions in fall into humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil in shade; Potsdam Stripe spreads by rhizome like other lily of the valley selections and naturalizes well in a shaded woodland setting.

directions: Plant pips or divisions in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil in shade; Potsdam Stripe is a variegated lily of the valley selection with longitudinal white-to-cream striping down each leaf, adding foliage interest to the classic fragrant small white bell flowers of spring. Like other Convallaria majalis cultivars it spreads steadily by underground rhizome to form a dense, long-lived groundcover under trees or along shaded path edges. All parts of the plant are toxic if ingested, so consider that before planting where children or pets have access.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in deep shade; like other Aspidistra sichuanensis selections, Amanogawa is extremely tolerant of dry shade and root competition once established.

directions: Plant in deep shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil; Amanogawa is a clumping cast iron plant selection with light speckling and striping typical of Aspidistra sichuanensis selections, grown for its tough, architectural evergreen foliage rather than its inconspicuous ground-level flowers. It tolerates deep shade, dry soil, and root competition from nearby trees better than almost any other broadleaf evergreen, making it a reliable problem-solver for the darkest, driest corners of a garden. Established clumps need little care beyond an occasional cleanup of old or damaged leaves.
